messages:
Sam: Heads-up — enabling FP8 on H100 with TE v2.3 exposed a perf regression on long-context workloads. p50 is fine, but p95 jumps ~2x. Anyone seen this pattern?

Anya: saw similar during Friday runs. p50 ~12ms, p95 ~95ms for seq=4096 on batch=8. Throughput drops ~18% vs INT8 baseline.

Mike: My preliminary flamegraphs point at repeated kernel fallback between te_fast_fp8 and te_fallback_int8 during KV replay. Extra memcpy + kernel launch thrash.

Sam: do you have the profiler trace?

Anya: pasted snippet from perf tool:
```
[seq=4096,batch=8] total_tokens=1.2M
kernel te_fast_fp8: 68% time, 18us/op
kernel te_fallback_int8: 22% time, 120us/op (lots of small launches)
KV replay memcpy: 9% time (hot paths at 0x7f8...)
```

Anya: note: fallbacks spike when KV-hit ratio < ~0.7 (lots of prompt re-tokens), seems like routing heuristic choosing wrong kernel for mixed seq lengths.

Mike: sounds like our kernel selector is choosing fp8 path if avg_seq < 512 but we see long tails. Need sequence-distribution aware heuristic.

Sam: can we try an adaptive heuristic: if P(seq>1024) > 0.1 then force conservative kernel + larger batching window?

Mike: proposed config I tested locally:
```json
{"kernel_selector": "adaptive", "seq_tail_threshold": 0.1, "tail_seq_cutoff": 1024, "max_batch_ms": 4}
```
Worked: p95 dropped back to ~48ms, throughput +6% vs previous fp8-enabled run.

Anya: great. Also found quant calibration magnifies this — our per-tensor scale estimation sometimes saturates heads with long sequences causing TE to switch to fallback kernels to preserve numerics. Reducing clip factor from 2.5->1.8 helped numeric stability and avoided fallback.

Sam: what's the knob to toggle calibration clip?

Anya: in calibration.json -> "clip_multiplier": 1.8. Example: `calibrate --model qlora-1b --mode=fp8 --clip=1.8`

Mike: FYI devops-bot noticed a pattern in infra logs where node reclaiming GPU memory triggers kernel fallback due to transient memory allocation failures (OOM vs fragmentation). That explains occasional spikes even with good seq distribution.

devops-bot: deploy-log: job/te-service-3 restarted 2026-03-15T08:13:22Z due to cudaMalloc failure; instance h100-16g-3 (kernel=te_fast_fp8) moved to fallback profile.

Sam: so root causes: 1) selector mispred for seq tail, 2) calibration clip causing numeric fallback, 3) infra fragmentation -> transient fallbacks.

Anya: short action list:
- update kernel selector to look at seq-tail percentile (p90/p95) not just mean
- change calibration default clip -> 1.8 for fp8 on H100/L40S (rollback safe)
- add grace on cudaAlloc failures: try one retry before global fallback, and track metrics

Mike: I'll open a small canary rollout: adapt-selector + clip=1.8 + retry-on-alloc. Canary config: 5% traffic on dedicated pool (h100), ttl 1h, collect p50/p95, kv-hit-rate.

Sam: add an eval run with synthetic long-context prompt set (repro script below) and include kv-hit toggles.

Mike: repro command: `./tools/run_bench --model ./models/galactica-fp8 --seq 4096 --batch 8 --kv-hit-rate 0.6 --kernel-selector adaptive --calib-clip 1.8`

Anya: I'll add perf dashboards — per-kernel invocation count, memcpy % time, fallback rate. Also alert if fallback_rate > 0.02 for >5m.

Sam: thanks. If canary looks good we can flip default for H100 and L40S. Also add a note to release notes about calibration change and opt-in flag for 4-bit kernels (they're still experimental). :eyes:

Mike: one more: for mixed precision path we should log the exact reason for fallback (numeric_safety | allocation | unsupported_op) so we can triage faster. Right now it's a generic "fallback".

Anya: yes — adding structured fallback_reason tags to traces now.

Sam: perfect. Assign owners? Mike: selector+canary; Anya: calibration+dashboards; Sam: release notes + rollout plan.

Mike: will push PR with tests and microbench results by EOD.

Anya: will add dashboards + alert rules.

Sam: thanks all. We'll sync tomorrow after canary. :thumbsup:
